newsitem.title: MALI: Anglo-American raises stake in West African gold.
newsitem.headline: Anglo-American raises stake in West African gold.

text.p: Anglo American Corp of South Africa Ltd has raised its West African mining exploration budget by $4 million for 1996/97 and aims to expand its existing gold mining interests outside Mali, said a spokesman for the South African mining group.

"Sadiola (West Africa's second largest gold mine) is for Anglo a gateway to West Africa," said exploration manager R.D. Corrans, adding that the regional exploration budget had been set at $19 million against $15 million in 1995/96.

"The mine will produce 10 tonnes of gold a year with 250 permanent employees," said mine director Roger Attridge, putting total project costs at $303 million -- shared by Anglo-American and the World Bank's International Finance Corporation.
Sadiola has estimated geological reserves of 140 tonnes.
Gold mining has expanded rapidly in Mali and other African countries since 1990 as governments have opened mining to foreign investment and South Africa's lustre has faded.
Industry analysts have predicted $100 million of South African mining firm investment in Africa in 1996/97 with Anglo-American spending $45 million on mainly grassroots projects.
Mali, one of Africa's poorest countries, introduced widespread democratic reforms and struck a peace with Tuareg rebels before Sadiola poured its first gold in December 1996.
Mali holds an 18 percent share in Sadiola (Societe des Mines d'Or Mines, SEMOS) and would earn 12 billion CFA a year from the project, mine manager Roger Attrridge told visiting reporters.
Regional gold-bearing geological structures underlying Sadiola could prove to be of world importance, Anglo-American business development manager Alan McKerron said this week.
Main shareholder Anglo-American manages Sadiola on behalf of its 38 percent shareholding partner, Canadian firm Iamgold.
Anglo-American has also raised its East African mining exploration budget for 1996/97, to $13.2 million from $11.8 million last year, said Corrans.
